facts.statement: Byronosaurus was a troodontid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus is a genus of troodontid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Michael Novacek discovered the first skeleton of Byronosaurus in 1993 at Ukhaa Tolgod in the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: In 1993, Michael Novacek, a member of an American Museum of Natural History expedition to the Gobi Desert, discovered the skeleton of a small theropod at Ukhaa Tolgod.

facts.statement: A second specimen, a skull, was discovered on July 15, 1996, at the Bolor's Hill site approximately eight kilometers from the original find.
facts.quote: On 15 July 1996, at the Bolor's Hill site, about eight kilometers (five miles) away from the original location, a second specimen was discovered, a skull.

facts.statement: In 2009, two juvenile skulls and lower jaws were reassigned to Byronosaurus after they had originally been identified as Velociraptor.
facts.quote: In 2009, two front skulls and lower jaws of very young, perhaps newly hatched, individuals, specimens IGM 100/972 and IGM 100/974, were referred to Byronosaurus, after originally having been identified as Velociraptor exemplars.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers suggested that juvenile specimens previously assigned to Byronosaurus actually belong to Almas ukhaa due to differences in skull features like the number of maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: In 2017, the researchers who described a troodontid Almas ukhaa suggested that the specimens described by Bever and Norell (2009) don't belong to Byronosaurus based on different features found in the skull such as the number of maxillary teeth in both specimens being significantly fewer than this genus.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus was a small dinosaur measuring 1.5 to 2 meters long, 50 centimeters tall, and weighing between 4 and 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus was a small dinosaur, measuring about 1.5 - 2 m long and 50 cm tall; it weighed only about 4 - 20 kg.

facts.statement: Unlike most troodontids, Byronosaurus lacked serrations on its teeth, a trait shared with its relative Xixiasaurus and considered a primitive feature.
facts.quote: Unlike most other troodontids, its teeth seem to lack serrations just like its closest relative Xixiasaurus, probably a plesiomorphic trait among troodontids.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus is classified within the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: familia: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Byronosaurus is tentatively placed in the subfamily Troodontinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Troodontinae?

facts.statement: Byronosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85 to 70 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 85 y 70 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Troodontids, including Byronosaurus, possessed some of the highest encephalization quotients among non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Troodontids had some of the highest encephalization quotients (a measure of the ratio between actual brain size and the brain size predicted from body size) among non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Large eye-sockets and well-developed middle-ears suggest that troodontids like Byronosaurus had keen senses.
facts.quote: As suggested by their large eye-sockets and well-developed middle-ears, they appear to have had keen senses.

facts.statement: Proportionately long legs indicate that troodontids like Byronosaurus were agile.
facts.quote: They also had proportionately long legs, which indicates they were agile.

facts.statement: In 2001, Philip J. Currie and Dong Zhiming argued that troodontids were carnivorous, noting their anatomy and serrated teeth were consistent with a meat-eating lifestyle.
facts.quote: In 2001, the palaeontologists Philip J. Currie and Dong Zhiming rejected the idea that troodontids could have been herbivorous. They stated that troodontid anatomy was consistent with a carnivorous lifestyle, and pointed out that the structure of their serrations was not much different from those of other theropods.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that the loss of serrations in Byronosaurus teeth indicates a dietary shift, possibly making these animals herbivorous or omnivorous.
facts.quote: Lü and colleagues discussed the previous studies of troodontid diet, and suggested that the loss of serrations in the teeth of Byronosaurus and some other troodontids was related to a change in their diet. Since the teeth would appear to have lost their typical ability to slice meat, at least these troodontids may therefore have been either herbivorous or omnivorous.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that juvenile Byronosaurus skulls found in an oviraptorid nest were washed there from a nearby Byronosaurus nest by water flow.
facts.quote: In 2011, Norell stated that the Byronosaurus nest was found two metres uphill from the oviraptorid nest, with the oviraptorid nest at the end of a drainage course from the Byronosaurus nest, suggesting that the baby Byronosaurus skulls must have been washed from one nest to the other.

facts.statement: Some researchers dispute the assignment of the juvenile skulls to Byronosaurus, citing skull morphology differences and suggesting they may not belong to the genus.
facts.quote: Not only is the claim regarding nest parasitism considered dubious, but other researchers have pointed out the differences in skull morphology, suggesting that these specimens do not belong to this genus.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus was a troodontid, a group of small and gracile maniraptorans similar to birds.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus era un trodóntido, un grupo de pequeños y gráciles maniraptoranos similares a pájaros.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus was a small and graceful dinosaur measuring 1.50 meters in length, 50 centimeters in height, and weighing 4 kilograms.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus es un pequeño y grácil dinosaurio de solo 1,50 metros de largo 50 centímetros de alto y 4 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus is one of the few troodontids that lack serrated teeth, similar to its closest relative Xixiasaurus.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus es uno de pocos trodóntidos que no tienen dientes aserrados, similar a Xixiasaurus su pariente más cercano.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus possessed a large brain relative to its body and hunted insects and small vertebrates like lizards, fish, and mammals with needle-like teeth similar to those of primitive birds, resembling Archaeopteryx in this regard.
facts.quote: Poseía un cerebro grande comparado con su cuerpo pero se diferencia de otros trodóntidos por sus dientes sin el aserrado típico, sino como agujas similares a los de las aves primitivas, con lo que cazaba insectos, y pequeños vertebrados como lagartos, peces y mamíferos, en este sentido se asemeja al Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus had forward-facing eye sockets that provided stereoscopic vision.
facts.quote: Sus cuencas oculares apuntan hacia el frente, dándole visión estereoscópica.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus had a nasal passage in its snout where air passed through nasal windows before entering the mouth, a feature similar to that found in birds.
facts.quote: Tiene un compartimiento en el hocico donde el aire pasa por las ventanas de la nariz antes de pasar a través de la boca, característica similar a la encontrada en los pájaros.

facts.statement: Two skulls of Byronosaurus have been found, one measuring 23 centimeters, representing the best-known troodontids to date.
facts.quote: De este dinosaurio se ha encontrado 2 cráneos, uno de ellos de 23 centímetros; son los mejores conocidos trodóntidos hasta la fecha.

facts.statement: The holotype of Byronosaurus was found in 1933 in Ukhaa Tolgod, Gobi Desert, Mongolia, in the Djadokhta Formation and illustrated as an undescribed troodontid in 1934 by Novacek et al.
facts.quote: El holotipo del Byronosaurus fue encontrado en 1933, en Ukhaa Tolgod, en el Desierto de Gobi en Mongolia en la Formación Djadokhta, fue ilustrado como un trodóntido sin describir en 1934 por Novacek et al.

facts.statement: The paratype was found in 1996 at Bolor Hill, 8 kilometers from the original site.
facts.quote: El paratipo se encontró en 1996 en la colina Bolor a 8 kilómetros del sitio original.

facts.statement: In 2000, Mark Norell, Peter Makovicky, and James Clark named and described the type species Byronosaurus jaffei.
facts.quote: En 2000, Mark Norell , Peter Makovicky y James Clark nombraron y describieron la tipo de Byronosaurus, B. jaffei.

facts.statement: The species name honors Byron Jaffe in recognition of his family's support for the expeditions of the Mongolian Academy of Sciences and the American Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie en su conjunto honró a Byron Jaffe, "en reconocimiento al apoyo de su familia a las Expediciones Paleontológicas de la Academia Mongola de Ciencias y el Museo Americano de Historia Natural".

facts.statement: The holotype, IGM 100/983, was found in a layer of the Djadochta Formation dating to the Late Campanian.
facts.quote: El holotipo , IGM 100/983, fue encontrado en una capa de la formación de Djadochta que data del Campaniano tardío.

facts.statement: In 2009, two frontal skulls and lower jaws of very young individuals, perhaps recently hatched, specimens IGM 100/972 and IGM 100/974, were referred to Byronosaurus after originally being identified as Velociraptor specimens.
facts.quote: En 2009, dos cráneos frontales y mandíbulas inferiores de individuos muy jóvenes, tal vez recién eclosionados, los especímenes IGM 100/972 e IGM 100/974, se refirieron a Byronosaurus, después de haber sido originalmente identificados como ejemplares de Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Mark Norell and colleagues described two juvenile specimens, neonates or embryos near hatching, of Byronosaurus, specimens IGM 100/972 and IGM 100/974, in 1994.
facts.quote: Mark Norell y colegas describieron dos ejemplares de perinatos, recién nacidos o embriones cercanos a la eclosión, de Byronosaurus, los especímenes IGM 100/972 e IGM 100/974 en 1994.

facts.statement: The two specimens were found in an oviraptorosaur egg nest in the Late Cretaceous "Flaming Cliffs" of the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Los dos especímenes se encontraron en un nido de huevos deoviraptorosáurido en la "Flaming Cliffs" del Cretácico Tardío de la formación Djadochta de Mongolia.

facts.statement: Hypotheses explaining how they ended up there include that they were prey for the adult oviraptorid, that they were there for oviraptorid chicks to exploit, or that an adult Byronosaurus may have laid its eggs in an oviraptorosaur nest in a case of brood parasitism.
facts.quote: Hipótesis que explican cómo llegaron a estar allí incluyen que fueron presas del oviraptórido adulto, que estaban allí para que las aprovechasen las crías de oviraptórido, o que un adulto Byronosaurus pueden haber puesto sus huevos en un nido de oviraptosáurido en un caso de parasitismo de puesta.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus has been considered a member of the family Troodontidae since 2000.
facts.quote: Byronosaurus es considerado desde el año 2000 un miembro de la familia Troodontidae.

facts.statement: Byronosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
